generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The double cast `(List<Alias>) (List)` is used to bypass Java's generic type checking. This circumvents compile-time type safety and introduces a risk of `ClassCastException` at runtime if `mergeOutputExpressions` returns any element that does not inherit from `Alias`.

Replacing the return of an `UnresolvedAttribute` with a thrown `IllegalStateException` changes the error handling from diagnostic collection to "fail-fast". In an analysis phase, this prevents the system from identifying and reporting multiple issues in a single pass, which degrades the user experience by requiring a trial-and-error approach to fix query errors.
The updated error message removes the helpful guidance on how to resolve the ambiguity ("to disambiguate use quotes or qualifiers"), making the error less actionable for the end user.

review_comment:
Actually, I changed my mind on this:

It is the actual name that needs to be unique; otherwise, bugs could slip in because we somehow end up using qualifiers on accident; qualifiers are not respected by our optimization rules, e.g. `mergeOutputAttributes`;  this [PR](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/110581) demonstrates that qualifiers are entirely unused, and the validation for the current state should reflect current assumptions.

If we end up using qualifiers after all (I think that's really for the future and we should really remove them until then), we can easily update the validation.
